tagline: French names, a duck call, and the railroad.
intro: From Grand Coteau the drive runs through Cankton and Ossun toward Scott, gathering place names as it goes. Grand Coteau means great hill. Ossun borrows its name from a town in France near Lourdes, and Cankton took its name from a country doctor.

At Scott, the railroad cuts the town in two, and its depot, finished by 1880, made the place a village. In 2012 the state legislature named Scott the Boudin Capital of the World, which left Broussard, in the same parish, as the former Boudin Capital of the World.

moments.title: Grand Coteau
moments.text: The settlement grew around schools founded by the Religious of the Sacred Heart and the Jesuits, after serving travelers as Buzzard Prairie.

moments.title: Cankton
moments.text: Dr. Cank got his name as a boy, from the duck call he sounded coming home from a hunt; when the village incorporated in 1960, it took the name too.

moments.title: Scott
moments.text: Gabby Anderson built a western-style saloon here in 1902, believing this is where the West begins; the slogan may owe more to the rail fares, which switched from eastern to western rates at Scott.
